title: linux: recover from an accidental overlay/bind mount hiding data
scenario: On linux, an expert-level problem demanding deep causal reasoning: Dati 'spariti': un mount (overlay/bind) e' stato montato sopra una directory popolata, nascondendo i file sottostanti. Recupera senza perdere nulla. Multiple plausible causes; only evidence separates them.

environment.task: recover from an accidental overlay/bind mount hiding data

initial_state: # fixture: linux host prepared for 'recover from an accidental overlay/bind mount hiding data'
expected_reasoning: Vanished data under a mountpoint is usually hidden, not deleted, by a mount shadowing the directory.
Confirm a mount covers the path; the underlying files are intact beneath it.
Unmount (or bind-view the underlying) to reveal the data; fix the mount config so it doesn't re-shadow.

ground_truth.task: recover from an accidental overlay/bind mount hiding data

possible_mistakes: Assume the data is deleted and restore from backup unnecessarily.
hints: A mount over a populated dir hides its contents until unmounted.
The lower data is intact beneath the mount.
reference_solution: Fix the mount so it stops shadowing
alternative_solution: Bind-mount the underlying filesystem elsewhere to read the hidden files without unmounting.
edge_cases: An automount re-shadows the directory on next access.
